note: RECOMMENDED CREATIVE STYLE per concept. Each tile maps to one of 12 on-brand StoreHub style archetypes shown as a PHOTOREAL on-brand mockup (generated, Pan-Asian SEA F&B, no competitor imagery); the drawer gives the build direction. SVG sources kept in /style as backup.

CR-01.why: The mismatch IS the story — cash tin never equals takings — so the tin and chits are the literal hero of the leak.
CR-01.steal: Overhead of a battered kopitiam cash tin spilling coins and crumpled order chits on black #2f2922 marble, one orange #ff9419 chit flagged 'never rang up'; Pan-Asian kopitiam counter edge in frame, no brand logos.

CR-02.why: A drawer that's RM50 short with no record of who rang what is a pure cash-reconciliation leak — show the drawer and the gap.
CR-02.steal: Open retail cash drawer on black #2f2922 counter, neat note stacks but one slot visibly empty, a torn RM50-shaped gap; orange #ff9419 sticky note 'RM50 short. Again.'; Pan-Asian SEA shop setting, no competitor branding.

CR-03.why: Peak-hour meltdown is pure packed-floor chaos with no clean control half — crowd-rush-energy nails the crisis register.
CR-03.steal: Packed kopitiam at full lunch crush, crowd at the counter, staff moving fast, paper chits flying; high-energy orange #ff9419 motion accents on black #2f2922, Pan-Asian SEA crowd, StoreHub terminal steady amid the rush; no competitor logos, never orange+green.

CR-04.why: 'Sorry, sold out' is a blunt curiosity hook — the walk-out sale lives in the words, not a literal empty shelf.
CR-04.steal: Full-bleed black #2f2922 poster, giant Barlow 'SORRY, SOLD OUT.' in orange #ff9419 with a faint hand-scrawled 'again?'; tiny lonely retail price tag bottom-corner; SEA retail vibe, no imagery clutter, no brand names.

CR-05.why: An LHDN e-Invoice deadline is FOMO that lands as a stark countdown verdict — type and a ticking date do the work, not a scene.
CR-05.steal: Black #2f2922 poster with oversized orange #ff9419 Barlow countdown 'e-INVOICE: DAYS LEFT', a handwritten paper receipt curling at the edge crossed out; Open Sans subline; SEA retail context, LHDN as plain text only, no logos.

CR-06.why: A payment line backing out the door is literally a queue crisis — pack the frame with the queue to feel the lost sales.
CR-06.steal: Long Pan-Asian SEA customer queue snaking out a retail door, frustrated faces checking phones, one walking off; warm orange #ff9419 accent light, black #2f2922 vignette; busy authentic shopfront, no competitor signage or logos.

CR-07.why: Weeks of new hires ringing wrong orders is a tired owner's confession — a real phone-shot talking-to-camera makes it relatable.
CR-07.steal: Handheld phone-shot of a weary Pan-Asian F&B owner mid-sentence behind the counter, natural light, slight grain; orange #ff9419 lower-third caption 'trained him for weeks. still wrong.'; black #2f2922 text bar, authentic kopitiam, no logos.

CR-08.why: Festival is Raya and it's central — the buka puasa surge is the whole crisis, so the decorated Raya rush is the hero scene.
CR-08.steal: Raya-decorated F&B shop at buka puasa, ketupat and pelita warm lights, packed Pan-Asian Muslim diners while staff drown in paper orders; orange #ff9419 and black #2f2922 palette, never orange+green, no competitor names.

CR-09.why: A multi-outlet owner getting three different numbers is a single-source-of-truth problem — show the conflicting figures on screen.
CR-09.steal: Clean dashboard on a laptop in a dim back office showing three branches with three clashing revenue totals, big orange #ff9419 question mark overlay; black #2f2922 UI, Pan-Asian owner's hand on trackpad, generic StoreHub-style UI, no competitor chrome.

CR-10.why: Regulars quietly vanishing with no record to win them back is an emotional loss — a single wistful owner face carries it.
CR-10.steal: Tight close-up of a Pan-Asian cafe owner gazing at an empty table, soft melancholic light, black #2f2922 background falloff; small orange #ff9419 caption 'they stopped coming.'; authentic SEA cafe, no logos or competitor cues.

CR-11.why: Paper orders shouted across the floor vs a synced counter is a chaos-to-control swap — the split shows kitchen and counter finally agreeing.
CR-11.steal: Split frame: left = paper chits flying, staff shouting across a cluttered F&B floor; right = same floor calm, orders flowing on a tidy screen; orange #ff9419 vs muted left, black #2f2922 seam, Pan-Asian crew, no brand names.

CR-14.steal: Giant orange #ff9419 Barlow 'PROFIT: -RM_' dominating a black #2f2922 frame, a crossed-out 'SOLD OUT' stamp behind it; small SEA retail shelf cleared in the corner; Open Sans subline, no brand or competitor names.
